claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the link target of the 'Provider support policy' card on the support index page).
The Pulumi provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Some Pulumi providers get long-term security updates, and the provider support policy page identifies which ones.
Pulumi's provider version support policy: Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi also ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The provider support policy page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry lists the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (Provider support policy).
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes if an error occurs during an update; it completes pending in-progress operations then exits and reports the error.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes and applies desired state in a single step.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine; some Pulumi providers use Terraform schemas, while native providers map directly to cloud APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers receiving long-term support updates are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
Registry package pages exist at /registry/packages/ for aws, azure, azure-native, azuread, command, docker-build, gcp, kubernetes, tls, and vault.

The LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches, including fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or direct dependencies, and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship them.
An LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
LTS providers remain compatible with the version of Pulumi they were frozen at unless security fixes require otherwise.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.
When N+1 ships, N becomes the current major's predecessor as the new LTS major, and the old LTS major reaches end of life the same day regardless of remaining 12-month window.
Within the LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases, but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and pinning to a major version is recommended.
Older majors than the LTS version receive no patches; if v3 is newest, v2 is N-1 and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major (N) receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
End-of-life versions (N-2 and older) are not supported and receive no updates.
The Pulumi support FAQ has a section 'what are the best practices for maintaining provider versions' at /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/.
Pages exist at /registry/ and /docs/support/getting-support/.
